fingerprint.command: names=$(amp tools list 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^  \([a-z_]*\) .*/\1/p') && [ -n "$names" ] && printf '%s\n' "$names" | sort | sha1sum | cut -c1-12
fingerprint.note: sha1 of the built-in tool names from `amp tools list`; it changes when Amp's tool set changes, not on every release. Observed with Amp CLI 0.0.1791907253 on 2026-10-13.

entry.context: Orb thread. Observed from an Amp orb whose agent ran as Claude Code (the Claude Agent SDK) with Amp's MCP tools; Amp-native tool names below come from `amp tools list`, the Amp docs, and the Amp MCP tool schemas, and were not all exercised in this session.
sources: Amp MCP tool schemas in session: create_thread, read_thread, get_thread_status, send_thread_message, find_thread, update_thread, ask_user_choice, list_agent_modes, upload_thread_file, download_thread_file, download_thread_changes, thread_file_url, set_schedule/get_schedule/update_schedule/clear_schedule (via tool_search), create_github_subscription
Official skills creating-artifacts and creating-views (materialized under ~/.cache/amp/global-skills/ampcode.com/official/)

owners.launch: `create_thread` with a prompt and an intent; optional `agent_mode` (built-in low, medium, high, ultra, or a plugin or custom mode key), `executor` orb (default: a fresh orb and checkout from the project's default branch) or a live runner by `runner_id`, optional `worktree` on a runner. Returns immediately with the thread ID; the new thread does not inherit this conversation or uncommitted files.
owners.inspect: `read_thread` answers a question against the thread's full history or its current context window; `get_thread_status` returns the agent state, mode, and any pending user-input dialog; `find_thread` searches threads by keyword, file name, author, label, or date. None of these wake the thread. On the web, the thread URL plus `.md` or `amp threads markdown T-…` exports it.
owners.message: `send_thread_message` to a thread the user owns or can contribute to; it wakes the thread and starts a turn. A message answers a pending `ask_user_choice` dialog unless the dialog is marked requiresHuman, in which case the message queues behind it. `amp threads continue T-… -ox '<message>'` does the same from a shell.
owners.collect: Ask the owner in its prompt to `send_thread_message` its result back to the coordinator's thread ID, or (Amp native agent) call `wait_for_threads` then `read_thread`. Use one path, not both. Files come back only by explicit transfer (see evidence).
owners.close: `update_thread` with `archived: true` on a thread the user owns, or `amp threads archive`. The URL and history stay readable; archiving a thread does not archive the threads it created; an archived orb is not resumed for file downloads.
owners.resume: `send_thread_message` to the same thread, or open its URL and prompt. A paused orb wakes with conversation, files, and services in place; it pauses again a few minutes after the agent finishes.

helpers.invoke: `Task` (Amp native agent) with a prompt and subagent type; several independent calls issued in one message run in parallel. The subagent works in isolation on the same orb filesystem and cannot talk to other subagents. The Librarian is a built-in read-only subagent for code search; `oracle` is a second-opinion model for reasoning, not a subagent.
helpers.collect: The subagent's final summary arrives as the tool result; the caller never sees its step-by-step work. A Task run in the background reports through a completion notification in the caller's thread. A Task started in the background instead returns immediately and reports through a completion notification in the caller's thread.
helpers.readonly: No readonly parameter is documented for Task. Hold a helper to read-only by instruction in its prompt; the Librarian subagent is read-only by design.
helpers.definitions: None. Amp has no named subagent definitions; a Task subagent takes its instructions from its prompt. To dispatch a definition file such as pstack-agents/<name>.md, give Task a prompt that states the file's absolute path and tells the subagent to read and follow it before the task.

monitoring.notifications: A background Task notifies the caller's thread when it completes. GitHub events reach a thread through `create_github_subscription` (CI results, PR and issue comments, new PRs or issues). A thread the coordinator launched does not notify on its own; it must be asked to message back.
monitoring.wait: `wait_for_threads` (Amp native agent) waits for named threads with a timeout and holds the caller; `get_thread_status` is the non-blocking check.
monitoring.wake: `set_schedule` saves one schedule and prompt on the current thread (one-time or repeating; one schedule per thread); when it fires Amp wakes the agent with a short message and `get_schedule` returns the prompt. Works while the thread is idle; an orb resumes if the task needs it. `update_schedule` and `clear_schedule` change or remove it; a failed run pauses the automation.

skills.load: Amp lists every discovered skill's name and description to the model and loads the rest of SKILL.md with the `skill` tool when the model invokes it or the user types `/<name>`. A skill's instructions apply to the thread that loaded it, not to subagents it spawns.
skills.brief: Pass applicable instructions explicitly; do not assume inheritance.
skills.locations: In precedence order, first name wins: ~/.config/agents/skills/, ~/.agents/skills/, ~/.config/amp/skills/, .agents/skills/ in the project and parent directories, .claude/skills/ in those directories, ~/.claude/skills/, ~/.claude/plugins/cache/, directories in amp.skills.path, the personal skills repository, the workspace skills repository, then official Amp skills. Local directories are searched five levels deep; repository skills must sit in an immediate child directory of the repository root. `amp skills repositories` lists the personal and workspace repositories with their clone commands.
skills.reload: `reload_skills` tool rescans local directories and fetches the latest personal and workspace skills into the running session; new threads fetch them automatically. `amp skills list` in a shell does not reload a session.
skills.frontmatter: Amp reads `name` and `description`. It reads `mode` as an agent-mode override, so a Cursor custom-mode `mode: true` is wrong rather than ignored; `icon`, `color`, and `reminder` are ignored. `disable-model-invocation` is not documented; the key is harmless and the skill stays model-visible. `mcpServers` declares a bundled MCP server.

instructions.user: ~/.config/amp/AGENTS.md and ~/.config/AGENTS.md; system-wide /etc/ampcode/AGENTS.md (or the macOS and Windows equivalents); the web app's Global AGENTS.md under personal Settings > Advanced and under Workspace Settings > Advanced. Workspace guidance is included before personal and repository guidance.
instructions.project: AGENTS.md in the working directory and each parent up to $HOME, always included; AGENTS.md in a subtree when the agent reads a file there; AGENT.md or CLAUDE.md as the fallback name in a directory with no AGENTS.md; @-mentioned files, with `globs` front matter loading only after a matching file is read. AMP_IGNORE_GUIDANCE_FILES skips matching files.

entry.ask_user: `ask_user_choice`: one question with 2 to 5 options and an optional free-text 'Other'; the thread blocks (and may sleep) until the user answers in a dialog. Amp's guidance allows it only when the user explicitly asked to be asked questions; otherwise questions go in the reply.

models.select: For an owner: `create_thread` `agent_mode` with a built-in mode (low, medium, high, ultra) or a plugin or custom mode key; a mode named by the user, a skill, or a guidance file counts as an explicit choice. For a helper: Task takes no model; a subagent's model is routed independently of the main agent, and roles are pinned in Settings > Mode Dial > Tune Modes. `oracle` is the separate reasoning model.
models.list: `list_agent_modes` returns the built-in effort rows, plugin modes, and custom agents this session may use; the /modes page shows current model routing.

evidence.transfer: `upload_thread_file` (one file up to 4 MiB into another thread's workspace), `download_thread_file` (one file from a running or paused thread), `download_thread_changes` (every changed file from a thread's latest Changes capture, no executor needed), `thread_file_url` (temporary links, 3 hours), or push a branch. A message or commit ID does not transfer files.
evidence.retain_before_close: Push a branch for commits; for uncommitted work, `download_thread_changes` still works after the thread is archived, but `download_thread_file` does not resume an archived orb.

artifacts.label: HTML page served from the orb through a portal
artifacts.present: Write a self-contained HTML file and serve it from the orb (`creating-artifacts` skill: `.amp/in/artifacts/pages/<slug>.html` plus its share script, or `amp orb service start` and `amp orb portal <port>`); the portal URL is the link to share, written as a Markdown link titled "amp-portal".
artifacts.update: Rewrite the same file in place; the link stays stable. Restart the service only when the server does not pick up the change.
artifacts.audience: People who can view the thread. `amp orb portal … access` or the Portal tab can open a public link for 1 hour to 7 days that does not grant thread access.
artifacts.interaction: Review widget on every portal HTML page: a signed-in viewer selects an element and sends a comment, which arrives in the thread as a user message starting "Portal page comment from".
limits: Opening a portal wakes a paused orb and resumes billing.
Browser requests between two portal hosts are not supported.
A direct sandbox host URL or a file:// path does not work for the user; only the portal URL does.

artifacts.label: Inline interactive view in the reply
artifacts.present: A fenced `amp-view` code block holding one self-contained HTML document, rendered inline in the reply in a sandboxed frame that follows the reader's theme (`creating-views` skill).
artifacts.update: Post a new reply with a new block; a block is not revised in place.
limits: No network: inline all CSS, JS, images, and data; chart libraries and web fonts cannot load.
No popups, storage, or form submission; about 720px wide on desktop and 360px on phones; keep source under 100 KB.

artifacts.label: Local HTML file in the orb
artifacts.present: Write the file under .amp/in/artifacts/ and link it with a file:// URI in the reply.
artifacts.audience: The agent only; the user cannot open file:// or localhost links from an orb.
limits: Not viewable by the user; use a portal page instead.

limitations: Workspace model: an orb thread is isolated (own orb, checkout, and context, started from the default branch); a runner thread shares the runner's directory or takes a git worktree via create_thread's worktree option. The coordinator picks at launch with executor and runner_id.

Task, oracle, wait_for_threads, and reload_skills were not exercised here: this session's agent ran as Claude Code inside the orb, which exposes `Agent` instead of Task and lacks oracle and wait_for_threads. Their descriptions come from `amp tools list`, the docs, and the existing harness profile.
The docs do not document the frontmatter keys `disable-model-invocation` or `mode`; Amp reads only `name` and `description` per the skills page.
The docs give no Task API: no model parameter, no readonly parameter, and no documented follow-up to a finished subagent.
A launched thread sends nothing back on its own; collection depends on the prompt asking it to message the coordinator or on wait_for_threads.
